results.evidence: Retry found only loop trips (Pasayten peakbagging multi-summit loops, Ptarmigan loops) and the 36-mile round-trip figure; no source states a car-to-car gain or loss for this out-and-back to Dot. The instructions forbid computing gain or setting loss equal to gain, so nothing is patched. What would settle it is a published trip report for this exact Slate Pass to Dot out-and-back that gives the total gain and loss.

Three Forest Service pages (the Slate Pass trailhead, Slate Pass trail and Harts Pass trailhead pages) say no fees are required and mention no Northwest Forest Pass, but they all come from one publisher. WTA's Slate Peak page lists a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass, and the PNT's Harts Pass trailhead page gives a $5/day fee or recreation pass. The sources still disagree. A statement from the Methow Valley Ranger District naming Slate Pass as a fee site or a non-fee site would settle it.

Retry searches found the Beckey 5.6-5.7 West Ridge rating and descriptions of the low-fifth-class East-West traverse, but no page gives an NCCS commitment grade (II or III) for East McMillan Spire. Some pages could not be read (403), including the Mountaineers route page. A published grade for this route, such as the Mountaineers route page or the Beckey guide entry, would settle it.

results.fact: Overview says both needles were first climbed together in 1932
results.evidence: When re-read, the 2003 AAJ enchainment account says 'Three routes were first ascents: The Rake, East Twin Needle, and Himmelhorn', which credits a new ROUTE (the east arete, II 5.10a), not the first ascent of the peak. So it does not contradict a 1932 ascent. The 1962 AAJ Southern Pickets article says only that 'the Twin Needles had been climbed', and Wikipedia gives the Aug 17 1932 Degenhardt/Martin/Strandberg ascent for 'Twin Needles' as a unit. No source says explicitly that the 1932 party stood on the EAST needle. A source naming the first ascent of East Twin Needle specifically would settle it.

results.fact: fa credits the 2003 enchainment party with this moderate South Route
results.evidence: The `fa` field names Wallace, Haley and Bunker (July 27 2003) for this South Route. The overview and the 2003 AAJ account say that party climbed the hard east arete (II 5.10a), a different line. No source names the first-ascent party for the South Route, and FAs may not be invented, so nothing is patched. What would settle it is a source naming who first climbed the South Route, or a decision to blank `fa`.

Within the row, best_season, seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow and access.closures all say mid-July to early September, and climate.summer and the approach variant also run into September. The header's 'Late Jul-Aug' is the only field that ends in August. Externally, a Southern Pickets trip from Terror Basin to Crescent Creek Basin that climbed Terror's West Ridge ran July 15-19, 2008, which is mid-July. The 1962 AAJ Southern Pickets article records first ascents in the same group made in mid-September. The header season and the two 'late July' starts are aligned to the mid-July to early-September window.

dist_km 31.4 (19.5 mi) matches a published ROUND-TRIP figure, not a one-way approach. The retry found only the ~4.5 mi roadbed and qualitative times for the approach, and no second source that gives a one-way distance to the Crescent Creek or Chopping Block camp matching the row's 6-7.5 mi. Two trip reports that each state the one-way mileage from Goodell Creek to the Chopping Block ridge camp would settle it.
